activity: watching a big game with family and friends
knowledge_domain: watching a big game with family and friends
story:
Eloise went to the big stadium with Mama and Papa. It was her favorite place. The field was green and wide. The seats were red and clean.

The game began. The crowd stood up and cheered. "Hooray! Hooray!" Eloise sat in her seat. All she could see was a big blue coat. The game was hiding behind it.

Then the people sat down. Eloise saw the players again. One player kicked the ball. The crowd jumped up. The blue coat came back. The game hid again.

Eloise tried something. When the people stood, she stood too. One, two, three, up! She could see the whole field. When they sat, she sat. One, two, three, down!

The people cheered and cheered. Eloise cheered too. She clapped her hands. That night, she dreamed of the green field and the happy crowd.

"One more cheer," she said in her sleep, "one, two, three!"

activity: to put on a coat and zip it up by themselves
knowledge_domain: to put on a coat and zip it up by themselves
story:
Wyatt put on his coat all by himself. But the coat looked wrong. One arm went in the hood! He pulled it out and laughed.

Mommy waited by the cart. "Ready for the store?" she asked. "Not yet!" said Wyatt. He shook the coat like a big feather. It fell flat and smooth. Now he could see the two arm holes.

He pushed one arm in. Then the other arm. It worked! He pulled the zipper tab down, up, down, up. Then he zipped it all the way to his chin. "I did it!" he said.

At the store, Wyatt bounced down the aisle. His coat was warm and zipped tight. He picked out a big red apple. "My coat did this," he told the apple.

activity: celebrating a birthday with family and friends
knowledge_domain: celebrating a birthday with family and friends
story:
It was Miles's birthday at the park. There was a big table with cake and juice. Mom put down a little glass of apple juice just for him.

Dad brought out the cake. It had four candles on top. Dad lit them with a match, far from Miles's hands. The flames were small and orange. They wiggled in the breeze. "Make a wish," said Mom. "Then blow," said Grandma.

Miles took a big breath. He blew at the candles. The flames bent over. But they came right back up. Miles tried again, a soft little puff. The flames just danced. His eyes got wet. "I can't do it," he said.

"You can," said Dad. "Try one big, long blow." Miles filled his cheeks. He blew as hard as he could. Whoosh. All four flames went out at once. Smoke curled up in thin gray ribbons. Everyone clapped and cheered. Grandpa laughed a happy laugh.

Miles begged to do it again. "Maybe next year," said Dad, "with five candles." They ate cake in the warm sun. The juice was cold and sweet. Miles looked at the candles, all dark and quiet now. "My breath did that," he said.

activity: watching a big game with family and friends
knowledge_domain: watching a big game with family and friends
story:
Maeve sat on the grass at the big field. Mama sat next to her. Uncle Dan was way out there, playing in the game. He was just a small dot from here.

Maeve wanted Uncle Dan to see her. She clapped her hands. She called, "Dan! Dan!" He did not look. The game was loud. People were cheering all around her. Her tummy felt funny. She wanted him to wave back.

Then Maeve found her red scarf in the picnic bag. She held it up high. She waved it and waved it. The scarf was big and red like an apple. It moved in the wind, way up over the crowd. Uncle Dan looked up. He saw the red scarf. He smiled and waved right at her. Mama said, "He sees you!"

Maeve skipped in a little circle on the grass. The scarf was still up high in her hand. She waved it one more time. Uncle Dan blew her a kiss.

activity: the rote number words from one to ten heard in counting songs and everyday counting
knowledge_domain: the rote number words from one to ten heard in counting songs and everyday counting
story: Madelyn went to the library in the morning. Her mom held her hand. Madelyn wanted ten books about ducks, but she could only find one. One duck book sat on the shelf. The rest did not want to be found. "They like to hide," said the librarian, Miss Polly. "Let's hunt together." Madelyn was not alone. Miss Polly tapped the shelf. A second book slid out. Thump! Madelyn tapped too. A third book slid out. Thump! She tapped again and again. Four, five, six. Thump, thump, thump! The books smelled like paper and old rain. Seven books now sat in her arms. Eight was under a chair. Madelyn reached down and grabbed it. Nine was behind the puppet box. Miss Polly lifted it out with a smile. "One more," said Miss Polly. Madelyn looked up. The tenth book was on top of the shelf. It was too high for her little hands. "May I?" asked Miss Polly. She reached up and took it down. Madelyn counted them all. "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten!" Ten duck books, warm in her arms. Mom found a soft rug. They sat down side by side. "Read the big one first," said Madelyn.

activity: basic color words such as red, blue, yellow and green
knowledge_domain: basic color words such as red, blue, yellow and green
story:
Charlotte went to the store with Dad. She wanted apples for snack time. "Let's try to find red ones," said Dad.

The store was big and bright. Charlotte saw yellow bananas first. Then she saw green grapes. "Not apples," she said.

She heard a cart wheel squeak. She heard a man call, "Blueberries here!" Charlotte walked with Dad down the fruit aisle. She touched a big round apple. It was red and smooth.

"Dad, this one!" she said. Dad put six red apples in the bag. Then they saw Mom's favorite things. "Mom likes blueberries," said Charlotte. "Can we get some?"

"Yes, good idea," said Dad. He put blueberries in the cart too.

At home, Dad baked pizza for lunch. The oven was hot, so Charlotte sat far away at her little table. She waited. Soon Dad brought out the pizza. He blew on her slice so it would not be hot for her.

Charlotte ate her pizza with red apple slices beside it. She held up a yellow cup. "Cheers, Dad," she said.
"Cheers, Charlotte," said Dad, and tapped her cup with his.

activity: to wash their hands with soap for twenty seconds before eating and after the toilet
knowledge_domain: to wash their hands with soap for twenty seconds before eating and after the toilet
story:
Michael ran to the table. Lunch was ready. His favorite sandwich sat on his plate.

"Hands first," said Mom. "Wash with soap."

Michael sighed. He wet his hands. He rubbed the soap. The bubbles felt smooth and slippery. Then he rinsed fast and ran back.

"Michael, look," said Mom. She held his finger under the light. A smudge of dirt was still there.

Michael looked at his sandwich. He looked at his finger. He ran back to the sink.

This time he rubbed and rubbed. He sang his song while he scrubbed. The bubbles covered both hands. He rinsed until his hands felt squeaky.

He held his hands up. Every finger was clean now. The dirt was gone.

He sat down and picked up his sandwich. His clean hands felt warm on the bread. He took a big bite.

"Good washing," said Mom. She gave him a thumbs up.

Michael smiled. Later, after the toilet, he ran to the sink all by himself. He rubbed the soap until more smooth bubbles grew. He sang his song again.

The soap bottle sat by the sink. Michael gave it a little pat, like planting a tiny high five on its side. Then he ran off to play, hands clean and smelling like flowers.

activity: polite and functional phrases such as please, thank you, sorry and asking for help
knowledge_domain: polite and functional phrases such as please, thank you, sorry and asking for help
story:
Sadie sat in her car seat. She wanted her red puzzle book. It was on the floor, far from her toes.

"Help, please, Mama," said Sadie. Mama reached back and got it. "Thank you," said Sadie. She smiled.

Sadie looked at the puzzle book. She tried to read the words. The words were too big. She turned the pages slowly, one by one.

Then her cup fell. It bumped Mama's arm. "Sorry, Mama," said Sadie. "That's okay," said Mama. They waited at a red light. It was long.

Sadie asked again, "Please, more water, Mama?" They stopped the car. Mama filled the cup. The water was cool. Sadie drank it all.

Then Mama pointed out the window. "Look, Sadie. Cows!" The cows stood by the fence. Sadie waved at them.

"Thank you for the water," said Sadie. She held her cup up high. "More cows, please!"

activity: to count a group of up to ten objects and say which of two groups has more
knowledge_domain: counting, comparing amounts, and shapes
fact: When you count a group of things, the last number you say tells how many there are. You get the same answer no matter which one you count first.
story:
At school, Ruby sat at the little red table. On the table was a string of shiny beads. Her teacher, Miss Pam, had put them there. Ruby wanted to know how many beads she had. She wanted to tell her friend Leo, who had a string too.

Ruby began to count. She lifted the string with both hands. "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven." She stopped. Was seven right? She was not sure. She turned the string around. She counted from the other end. "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven." Seven again! "Did I get the same number?" Ruby asked herself. "Yes," she said. "Seven. It is seven both ways."

Then Leo held up his string. "Which one has more?" he asked. Ruby counted Leo's beads. "One, two, three, four, five." She looked at her own string. "Mine has more," she said. "Seven is more than five." Leo nodded and smiled.

Ruby counted her beads once more, just to see. "Seven," she said softly. The shiny beads clicked together on the string. Outside, a bird sang at the window. Ruby put her string down next to Leo's. His looked short. Hers looked long. "Mine is longer, too," said Ruby.

activity: going on a family trip away from home
knowledge_domain: going on a family trip away from home
story:
Lea packed her little red bag. In went her hat, her shell, and her duck. "We go far away today," said Mama. "The beach is not near our house."

The car ride was long. Long, long, long. Lea looked out the window. "Everything looks different here," she said. "The trees are different. The houses are different."

At last they reached the beach. Lea took off her shoes. The sand was warm. She ran to the water with her duck. She set the duck on a little wave. The duck sat on top. The duck did not sink. The water lifted it up and up.

"It floats!" said Lea. "Duck, you float!" She pushed the duck again and again. Each wave came in, and each wave took the duck back to her. Papa laughed. "The waves bring your duck home, just like our car brings us home." Lea hugged the wet duck. "You had a trip too," she whispered. "A big, wet trip." The next wave came in, and Lea jumped over it with a splash.

activity: learning to play a musical instrument
knowledge_domain: learning to play a musical instrument
story:
Athena sat by the piano at Miss Rosa's studio. She wanted to play a whole song. But her little fingers pressed two keys at once. The sound was big and jumbled. "That is not my song," said Athena. "Why does it sound muddled?" Miss Rosa smiled. "Try one finger at a time," she said. "Then you will hear."

Athena looked out the window. The sky was stormy and gray. Rain tapped on the glass, tap, tap, tap. Athena listened to the rain. Then she pressed one key. One finger made one clear note. She pressed another key. Another clear note came out. "One finger makes one sound!" said Athena. She laughed and did it again.

Then came a surprise. Athena played her notes slowly, one by one, and the taps of the rain seemed to play along with her. Miss Rosa clapped her hands. "That was lovely," she said. "You played a real song." Athena pointed at the big picture on the wall. It showed a piano with rain around it. "Rain and piano," said Athena.

At home time, Athena gave Miss Rosa a hug. "Thank you," said Athena. "Can we play more next time?" "Yes," said Miss Rosa. Athena waved and called out, "Bye, piano! Bye, rain!" The rain kept tapping on the window all the way to the car.

activity: planting a vegetable garden and watching it grow
knowledge_domain: planting a vegetable garden and watching it grow
story:
Nolan ran to the community garden with a little shovel. "Today we plant seeds!" he said. Grandma had three carrot seeds in her hand. The soil was brown and soft. Nolan poked a hole. He dropped a seed in. He patted it down smooth.

"Will it grow today?" Nolan asked. Grandma said, "No, it needs rain and sun first." Just then, drip, drip, drop! Rain fell on the garden. Nolan felt wet dots on his nose. He laughed. The rain made little ponds in the dirt.

The next day, the sun came out. Nolan looked at his pot. A tiny green leaf was poking up! "Look, look!" he shouted. He had made a hole, put in a seed, and now a plant was growing. Nolan ran to the water pump. "Grow, little carrot, grow!"

activity: cooking or baking a meal for the family
knowledge_domain: cooking or baking a meal for the family
story:
Theodore went to the farmers' market with Dad. "Apples for our pie!" said Dad. Theodore picked a big red one. He put it in the basket. The basket was getting heavy.

At home, Theodore had a job. He would help bake the pie. Dad cut the apples with a sharp knife. Theodore stayed back and watched. He was safe.

Then Theodore stirred the apple pieces in a big bowl. He added sugar and cinnamon. Stir, stir, stir! The apples got all covered in brown sugar.

Dad rolled the dough flat. Theodore pressed it into the pan. "Now the apples," said Dad. Theodore poured them in. They made a mountain of apples.

Then Dad put the pie in the hot oven. Theodore watched from his chair. He could not wait.

Soon the kitchen smelled like sweet apples. "Sniff, sniff!" said Theodore. Dad tapped the pie crust. "Knock, knock," it went. "It is ready!" said Dad.

The pie came out golden and warm. Theodore took a big bite. The apples were soft and sweet now. They had been hard before. Baking had changed them! Theodore roared like a happy lion and jumped up tall.

"Frozen ice cream for pie!" said Dad. Theodore clapped his hands. "Yes! Ice cream on my warm pie!"

activity: spending a surprise snow day at home
knowledge_domain: spending a surprise snow day at home
story:
Lucy woke up and looked out her window. Everything was white. "Snow!" said Lucy. "No school today," said Mama. "It is a snow day."

Lucy put on her warm red coat. She put on her boots and her mittens. Then Lucy, Mama, and Daddy walked to the big sledding hill. Lucy saw a little brown leaf on the snow. It looked so funny on all that white.

Lucy sat on her sled on the flat snow. She pushed and pushed. The sled did not go. Then Daddy said, "Let's try the hill." Lucy sat on the sled at the top. Daddy gave one little push. The sled went zoom, all the way down.

Lucy laughed and laughed. She ran back up the hill. She sat down again, and zoom, down she went. "The hill makes my sled go fast!" said Lucy. Then she went down one more time, with her arms out like wings.

activity: making an art or craft project
knowledge_domain: making an art or craft project
story:
Maverick sat at the little table. He had a big white paper and two paint pots. One pot was yellow. One pot was blue.

"I want green paint," said Maverick. "Where can green come from?"

Miss Rosa smiled. "Try mixing and see."

Maverick dipped his brush in yellow. He made a yellow cat with a long tail. Then he dipped the same brush in blue. He made a blue ball for the cat.

The yellow brush touched the blue paint. The blue pot turned green where the brush went in! Maverick opened his eyes wide. Yellow and blue had made green.

He counted his new paint. "One green, two green, three green spots."

Then he painted a big green grass. The yellow cat could sit on the green grass with his blue ball.

His friend Poppy had no paint left. Maverick gave her his green brush. "Here, you can use it."

"Thank you," said Poppy. "That is very kind."

Miss Rosa hung both pictures on the wall. The yellow cat smiled from the green grass.

activity: to throw a beanbag into a hoop and catch a large ball with both hands
knowledge_domain: to throw a beanbag into a hoop and catch a large ball with both hands
story:
Brielle ran into the sunny backyard. A red hoop sat on the grass. A big blue ball sat by her feet. Papa held a little beanbag.

"Try it," said Papa. "One, two, throw!"

Brielle threw the beanbag. It went up, up, and over the hoop. It landed in the grass behind it.

"Again," said Brielle.

"One, two, throw!"

This time she held the beanbag low. It went up and dropped right into the hoop. The hoop wobbled and the beanbag stayed in.

"I did it! I did it!" said Brielle.

"Now the ball," said Papa. "Hold out both hands."

Papa blew a whistle. The sound was loud and bright. He rolled the big ball to her.

Brielle held out one hand. The ball bounced off her fingers and rolled away.

"Both hands," said Papa. "One, two, catch!"

Brielle held out both hands. The ball rolled right in. Her two hands squeezed it and it stopped. It did not roll away.

"One, two, catch!" said Brielle. She caught it again. And again. And again.

"Big catch!" said Papa. He clapped his hands.

Brielle hugged the big blue ball and laughed.

"One, two, throw!" she said, and tossed it back to Papa.

activity: weather words such as sunny, rainy, windy and snowy and the clothes that go with them
knowledge_domain: weather words such as sunny, rainy, windy and snowy and the clothes that go with them
story:
Claare wanted to play outside. She stood at the front door and looked out.

The sun was shining. "It is sunny today!" said Claire. She put on her sun hat.

Then the wind blew. It blew her hat right off her head. The hat rolled on the grass. "Oh no!" said Claire. Her dad ran and caught the hat. "It is windy too," he said.

Then gray clouds came. Rain began to fall. Drip, drip, drop. "It is rainy now," said Claire. Puddles grew by the step. Claire put a leaf in the puddle. The leaf floated like a little boat.

The rain stopped. The sun came back. Claire saw something white on the ground. It was a small pile of old snow. The sun shone on it. The snow got smaller and smaller. Then it began to melt. Soon there was only a wet spot.

Claire put on her boots and her coat. Dad held her hand. They stepped outside together.

"Sun, wind, rain, and snow," said Claire. "All in one day!"

"Yes," said Dad, and he spun her hat onto her head.

activity: to share a toy with a classmate and wait for a turn without grabbing
knowledge_domain: to share a toy with a classmate and wait for a turn without grabbing
story:
Layla saw the big red truck. Ben had it first. He pushed it across the carpet.

Layla wanted the truck. She reached out and grabbed the back. The truck stopped. It would not go. Ben held on, and Layla held on, and the wheels did not turn at all.

Layla let go. She sat down and put her hands in her lap. Ben pushed the truck again. Now it rolled fast, all the way to the wall. Layla watched the wheels spin.

"The truck goes far when I share it," Ben said. He rolled it to her. Layla caught it with two hands.

"You can have a long turn," she said. "I need to wrap a present at the art table first." Layla carried her present back and showed it to Ben. Then he rolled the truck to her again.

activity: searching for a lost favorite toy
knowledge_domain: searching for a lost favorite toy
story:
Ibrahim went to the park with his mama. He had his red truck in his hand. But when he ran to the swings, his hands were empty. "My truck is lost," he said.

Ibrahim began to search. He looked under the bench. He only found a wet leaf there. He looked by the big tree. He found a smooth brown nut. No truck. The grass felt cold on his knees. His nose felt cold too, like winter was near.

Then Ibrahim saw the wind blow. The wind made a pile of dry leaves tumble over. The leaves rolled and skipped across the grass. Something red peeked out under the last leaf. It was his truck!

He tried to grab it, but the wind pushed one more leaf on top. Ibrahim laughed. He picked up the leaf first, then the truck. He held it up high. "Mama, the wind helped me find it!" he said. The wind blew again and ruffled his hair, soft and cool.

activity: to turn on a tablet, open a drawing app and put it away when done
knowledge_domain: to turn on a tablet, open a drawing app and put it away when done
story:
Leah sat on the big rug in the living room. She wanted to draw a cat. Her paper and crayons were all gone. But the tablet was on the table.

Mom picked up the tablet. She held it and pressed the little round button. The screen lit up with colors.

"Can I do it?" Leah asked.

"You can try," said Mom.

Leah pressed the round button too. The screen lit up again! Her finger made that happen.

She found the little paint pot picture. She tapped it with one finger. The drawing app opened. A big white page was there, waiting.

Leah drew a cat. She drew orange ears and a long tail. She drew tiny whiskers, one by one. The cat looked sleepy, so she drew a bed under it. She drew a yellow sun up high, because cats like warm spots that are not too hot.

"Mom, look at my cat!" said Leah.

"What a soft, sleepy cat," said Mom.

Leah was done now. She knew just what to do. She pressed the button again, and the screen went dark. She laid the tablet on the table, flat and safe.

"All put away," said Leah. She patted the tablet, just like she patted her cat.

activity: learning to play a musical instrument
knowledge_domain: learning to play a musical instrument
story:
Theo went to the community center with his dad. There was a music room there. On the wall hung little drums, bells, and a big drum.

A teacher named Ms. Rosa said, "You can pick one." Theo picked a little drum. He wanted to make it go boom. He sat on the floor and looked at it. He patted the drum very softly. The drum made a tiny sound. Tap, tap.

Theo wanted a big sound. He looked at the drumsticks. He took one in each hand. He lifted his arms up high. Then he brought them down fast. Boom! The drum made a big sound. Theo sat very still. He tapped soft again. Tap. He hit hard again. Boom!

He tried it on the bells, too. A soft touch made a little ring. A big swing made a loud ding. Theo smiled at his dad. "I can make it loud," he said. He tapped his favorite drum one more time. Boom, boom, boom. Outside the window, a duck waddled by on the grass.

activity: attending a religious or cultural celebration with family
knowledge_domain: attending a religious or cultural celebration with family
story:
Isabelle went to the big hall with Mama and Papa. It was a rainy day, so they hurried inside. There were lanterns and flowers everywhere. Today was a special celebration.

Isabelle saw a little clay pot with water in it. Grandma dipped a flower in the water. Then Grandma touched the flower to Isabelle's head. The water felt cool and soft. "Can I do that too?" Isabelle asked. "Yes, you can try," said Grandma. Isabelle dipped the flower in the water. The flower came out wet. She touched it to Mama's head. Mama smiled.

Then Grandma lit a little lamp with a match. Papa kept Isabelle back, safe. The lamp made the whole corner glow. Isabelle held Mama's hand and watched the light dance. "The lamp makes it bright," said Isabelle. Grandma hugged her close.

activity: cooking or baking a meal for the family
knowledge_domain: cooking or baking a meal for the family
story:
David put on his little apron. He was at school, in the cooking room. Today he would make bread for his family. Teacher Maya stood right beside him.

David mixed flour and milk in a big bowl. He made a soft ball of dough. Then he patted it flat. It looked small and sad. "Will this be enough for Mom and Dad?" he asked. Teacher Maya said, "We will give it time. Watch what happens."

They set the dough on the warm shelf by the oven. David read a book about a fox while they waited. The fox found berries that smelled sweet. David peeked at his dough. It had grown! It was big and puffy now. Teacher Maya put the pan in the oven, because ovens are hot.

Soon the bread came out, all golden. David carried it home in a box. Mom cut a slice. Dad took a bite and smiled. "This bread tastes sweet, like honey," said Dad. David patted his tummy and laughed.

activity: welcoming a new baby brother or sister into the family
knowledge_domain: welcoming a new baby brother or sister into the family
story:
Florence put her crayons in her little bag. She was going to the hospital to meet the baby. "I will draw the baby a picture," she said.

At the hospital, Mummy held a small bundle. A tiny face peeked out. "This is your baby brother," said Daddy. Florence drew a picture of a cat and a mouse. She held it up. The baby's eyes opened wide. He looked and looked. Then he waved his small hand. "He likes it!" said Florence. "The picture makes him look!"

Florence drew another picture. This time she drew a ball. She held it up. The baby waved again. "Again!" said Florence. Mummy laughed. "The baby is watching you," she said. Florence drew one more picture, slowly this time. It was the whole family, even the cat. The baby made a small sound, like a coo. Florence leaned close, very gently. "That is you," she whispered. "And that is me. I got that part wrong, but I fixed it." She pointed to her own smiling face, with its big round cheeks, drawn just right.

activity: to spread butter on toast and pour milk into a cup without spilling
knowledge_domain: to spread butter on toast and pour milk into a cup without spilling
story:
Ali ran into the big kitchen. The tables were long and wide. Toast was waiting on a plate. Soft butter sat in a little bowl. Ali wanted to make his own toast today.

He held the spoon. He patted the butter on the bread. He pushed too hard. The toast slid away! The cook, Ben, laughed. "Try soft hands," said Ben. Ali tapped the butter, soft like snow falling. The butter made a yellow coat on the toast. It looked so cute.

Next came the milk. Ali lifted the cup with two hands. He poured slow, slow, slow. Milk went up, up, up. Not one drop spilled! Ben gave him a thumbs up. Ali blew on the milk like it was hot cocoa, just for fun. Then he took a big bite of his toast. "More please!" said Ali.

activity: the idea that printed words carry meaning and that books are read front to back
knowledge_domain: people's jobs and how a community works
fact: At a library, you can borrow books and take them home, but you must bring them back by a certain day so other people can read them too.
story:
Eva went to the library with Mama. She saw a book about a little bear. The cover had shiny gold words. "Those words say bear," said a big girl next to her. Eva touched the words. Words talk to you, she thought. Like magic!

Eva opened the book. She turned the pages one by one. Front to back, front to back. The bear found honey on the very last page. "I love this book," said Eva. "I want to keep it forever and ever."

The library lady smiled. "You can take it home. But you must bring it back. Other kids want to read it too." Eva hugged the book tight. At home, she read it to her teddy. She read it to her socks. Then she read it one last time. "Come on, teddy," said Eva. "Time to take our book back to the library."

activity: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
knowledge_domain: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
story:
Leah wanted to play house at school. But the doll corner was full. The big plastic baby doll was already in Ben's arms.

Leah sat down to watch. Ben wrapped the doll in a scarf. Then he made a small crying sound. "Wah, wah," he said. "The baby is hungry."

Leah had an idea. She ran to the sand table. She filled a small bucket with pretend food. She carried it back, but the bucket was hard to hold. Rice bits fell out on the floor.

"Wait," said Ben. He put the baby in the toy cradle. Then he scooted over and held the bucket with her.

"You feed her first," said Leah. She held a wooden spoon to the doll. Ben patted the doll's back. The crying sound stopped.

"Now she is full," said Leah. "Now she can sleep." Ben tucked the scarf in tight. The baby closed her eyes, because Ben blinked them shut with his fingers.

"Tomorrow you can feed her first," said Ben. Leah smiled and picked up the empty bucket.

activity: welcoming a new baby brother or sister into the family
knowledge_domain: welcoming a new baby brother or sister into the family
story:
Everly was at Grandma's house. A new baby sister was coming home today. Everly wanted to give the baby a present. But what could a baby use?

She looked in Grandma's kitchen. Grandma was going to cook soup. The pot was hot, so Grandma stirred it herself. Everly stood back and watched. The soup smelled warm and good.

Then Everly saw something. Grandma blew on a spoon of soup. The soup was too hot. When she blew, the soup got cool. The baby could not eat hot food. Everly knew what to make.

"Grandma, can I have a bowl?" she asked. "Yes, dear," said Grandma. Everly found a little blue bowl. She put it on the table. She blew into the bowl, whoosh, whoosh. It felt cool inside. "This bowl is for the baby," she said.

The door opened. Mama came in with the baby. Everly held up the bowl. "The baby can have cool food," she said. Mama smiled big. Grandma gave the baby a soft little spoon too.

Everly sat close and watched her sister. The baby yawned. Everly whispered, "I made that for you."

activity: basic emotions such as happy, sad, angry, scared and excited
knowledge_domain: basic emotions such as happy, sad, angry, scared and excited
story:
Nova ran to the block corner at daycare. She wanted to build a big tower. Taller than her! She stacked one block, then two, then ten. Her tummy felt bouncy and light. She was so excited.

Then Ben grabbed the bottom block. The tower fell down with a crash. Nova's face got hot. She stomped her foot. "My tower!" she yelled. Ben's lip wobbled. He looked sad and backed away.

Nova felt bad now too. Then she heard a small sound. It came from the doll corner. Little Mia was hiding under the table. She was afraid of the loud crash. Nova crawled over. "It was just blocks," she said softly. "You can stay by me." Mia came out and held Nova's hand. Miss Amy smiled at them. "Nova, your tooth is showing," she laughed. Nova laughed too. Then all three friends built a new tower together. Mia put the top block on. It stayed tall. Nova clapped and clapped.

activity: polite and functional phrases such as please, thank you, sorry and asking for help
knowledge_domain: polite and functional phrases such as please, thank you, sorry and asking for help
story:
Mason wanted his red lion cup. It was up on the big shelf. He reached and reached. His fingers could not touch it.

Mason tugged the shelf. It began to shake. The cup wobbled. "Mason, stop," said Mom. She held his hand. "The shelf could tip over. Ask me for help instead."

"Help, please," said Mason. Mom smiled. She lifted the red lion cup down. "Here you go." "Thank you," said Mason. He hugged the cup to his chest.

"I am sorry I shook the shelf," he said. "That's okay," said Mom. "Asking for help is the polite way." Mason took a drink. The water was cold and good. Mom kissed the top of his head.

Mason held up the cup. "Roar," he said. Mom laughed and roared back.

activity: simple object categories such as animals, toys and foods
knowledge_domain: simple object categories such as animals, toys and foods
story:
Weston ran into daycare. He wanted to find his toy truck. But the toy shelf was empty. "Where did the toys go?" he asked.

Miss Rosa smiled. "The toys are all mixed up. Can you help sort them?" She held up a little dog. "This is an animal. Animals go in this basket." Weston looked. He saw a cat and a bunny. He put them in the animal basket too.

Then he found a ball. Balls are toys. He put the ball with the blocks and his truck. The truck was there! He held it tight.

Next came snack time. Miss Rosa put crackers in one bowl. She put apple slices in another bowl. "Foods go here," she said. Weston ate a sticky apple slice. Then he picked up his truck again.

"Animals in this basket," he said. He put the bunny in. "Toys here too." The shelf looked neat now. Miss Rosa clapped. "Good sorting, Weston." He smiled and rolled his truck on the rug.

activity: polite and functional phrases such as please, thank you, sorry and asking for help
knowledge_domain: polite and functional phrases such as please, thank you, sorry and asking for help
story:
Violet ran to the swing. It was her favorite swing, the red one. But when she got there, a boy was already on it. Violet felt like crying.

She took a big breath. "Can I have a turn, please?" she asked. The boy looked at her. "Okay," he said. "You can go next." He hopped off and held the rope. "Thank you," said Violet.

She swung up high. Her hat blew right off! "Help, Dad!" she called. Dad picked up the hat and put it back on her head. "Your hat is itchy," he said with a smile. He helped her zip her jacket up tight so the hat would stay.

Then Violet bumped into the boy by the slide. "Sorry," she said. The boy laughed. "It's okay! Want to slide together?" Down they went, one, two, whoosh!

activity: going on a family trip away from home
knowledge_domain: going on a family trip away from home
story:
Sienna sat by the train window with her mama. They were going to Grandma's house for a family trip. Sienna held her teddy bear in her lap. In her other hand she held a chocolate from Grandma's gift box.

"Look out the window," said Mama. So Sienna looked. One cow. Two sheep. Three little houses. "One cow. Two sheep. Three houses," said Sienna. The train went clickety-clack, clickety-clack.

The sun came in through the window. It made a warm patch on Sienna's knee. The warm patch sat right on her chocolate. Sienna squeezed the chocolate. It was soft and squishy now. "Oh," said Sienna. "The sun made my chocolate melt." It went gooey between her fingers like warm honey.

Mama laughed softly and wiped Sienna's hand with a fresh, clean napkin. Then Mama reached into her bag. "Look what else I have," she said. It was a small cool box. Inside was a cold yogurt drink. Sienna touched it. It was not warm at all, because it had stayed in the shade of the bag.

Sienna looked at the window, then at her empty wrapper. The sun made things melt. The shade kept things cool. She put the wrapper under her teddy bear, safe and tucked in. Then she counted again out the window. "One cow. Two sheep. Three houses. Four trees!" Then she saw something new by the fence. "Mama, look! A little goat is waving at me!"

activity: the idea that printed words carry meaning and that books are read front to back
knowledge_domain: people's jobs and how a community works
fact: At a library, you can borrow books and take them home, but you must bring them back by a certain day so other people can read them too.
story:
Aaron was staying at Grandma's house. Grandma had a library book. It was about big red trucks. It was Aaron's favorite book.

"Can I keep it forever?" Aaron asked.

Grandma shook her head. "The book has to go back. Other kids want to read it too."

Aaron held the book tight. He did not want to give it up. Then he turned the pages, one by one. The words on each page told the truck story. Grandma pointed to the first page. "We start here," she said. "Then we go to the back."

Aaron saw the words make the story. The front came first. The back came last.

Soon it was time to hurry. The book was due today. Aaron put it in his bag. He and Grandma walked to the library together.

Aaron gave the book to the library lady. "Other kids will read it now," she said.

"Can we get it again?" Aaron asked.

"Yes," said Grandma. "And we can take a new one home."

Aaron picked a book about trains. He hugged it all the way home.

activity: going to the dentist for the first time
knowledge_domain: going to the dentist for the first time
story:
Willow sat in the car with her teddy bear. They were going to the dentist. "First time," said Daddy. Willow held teddy tight. "What if it hurts?" she asked.

"Let's practice," said Daddy. "Open your mouth wide." Willow opened her mouth wide. "Now say ahh." Willow said, "Ahh." Daddy looked inside. "I see all your teeth," he said. "You opened wide, so I can see. That is smart." They practiced again. "Open wide. Say ahh." Willow did it one more time.

At the dentist, the chair was big and went up. Willow sat on it. The dentist said, "Open wide." Willow opened her mouth wide. She said, "Ahh." The dentist looked at all her teeth. Then Willow gave teddy a turn. "Open wide, teddy," she said. "Say ahh."

activity: making an art or craft project
knowledge_domain: making an art or craft project
story:
Joshua sat at the big table at camp. He had glue and paper and bits of yarn. He wanted to make a hat for his teddy bear. But the yarn would not stick. The pieces slid off the paper and fell to the floor.

Then Joshua put lots of glue on one bit of yarn. He pressed it down with his whole hand. He counted to ten in his head. He lifted his hand, and the yarn stayed put. "Look, Miss Amy!" he said. "It stayed!" Miss Amy smiled. "That is a good strong hat," she said.

Joshua added a red feather on top. The feather stuck too, because the glue was still wet. He put the hat on his teddy bear. Then he held the bear up high. "Now you can sing at camp!" Joshua said. The bear wore his hat all afternoon.

activity: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
knowledge_domain: pretend play scenarios such as playing house, caring for toys and role-playing simple situations
story:
Gabriella went to Mia's house. Mia had a big doll named Rosie. Rosie was crying, Mia said. "She needs a mama."

Gabriella picked Rosie up. She patted Rosie's back. Rosie kept crying. Then Gabriella wrapped Rosie in a soft blanket. The crying stopped. Mia clapped. "You made her sleepy!"

Then the dolls wanted to swim. Mia filled a small tub with cool water. The dolls dipped in. "Their skin gets wet and shiny," Gabriella said. She dried each doll with a tiny towel.

Next they played bakery. Gabriella spotted a spotted cat under the table. "A customer!" she said. She gave the cat a pretend cake. The cat licked its lips and purred.

Mia's mom brought real crackers. "Snack time for mamas too," she said. Gabriella rocked Rosie one more time, and Rosie's eyes closed tight.

activity: the idea that printed words carry meaning and that books are read front to back
knowledge_domain: people's jobs and how a community works
fact: At a library, you can borrow books and take them home, but you must bring them back by a certain day so other people can read them too.
story:
Asher went to the store with Mama. In the corner stood a little book shelf. "One book, two books, three books," said Asher. He counted them all.

He picked a soft book about a red truck. The cover had words on it. "T-R-U-C-K," said Asher. Mama read the words out loud. "It says truck!" Asher smiled big.

Asher sat on the floor. He opened the book at the front. He turned page one, page two, page three. Front to back. Front to back. "Not the back first," he said. "Front first!" That made Mama laugh.

The lady at the desk stamped the book. "Look," said Mama. "A day is on the stamp." Asher touched the stamp. The book had to go home with them for now. But it could not hide under his bed forever. It had to come back on the stamp day, so other kids could read it too.

Asher hugged the red truck book. "You visit me," he said. "Then you visit a friend." On the stamp day, Asher put the book in his bag. He carried it back all by himself. A small girl took it next. She opened it at the front. "Truck!" she said.

activity: hosting a grandparent who comes to stay for a week
knowledge_domain: hosting a grandparent who comes to stay for a week
story:
Grandma came to stay for a whole week. Eleanor wanted to give her a present on the very first day. But what could she give? She looked around the backyard. She saw a tiny yellow flower. She picked it and put it in a cup of water. Then she put the cup on the table in the middle of the yard.

The sun came out. It shone on the cup all day. Eleanor skipped over to look. The flower had opened wide, like a little sun itself. "Grandma, come see!" she called.

Grandma looked at the flower. "It opened for the sun," Eleanor said. She turned the cup so the flower faced Grandma's chair. "Now it can look at you." Grandma smiled and sat down in the sun too.

activity: making an art or craft project
knowledge_domain: making an art or craft project
story:
Cooper sat at the little table. He wanted to paint a big sun. He got a brush and some yellow paint.

Then the bell rang. It was noisy. Cooper jumped, and his brush fell. It landed right in his cup of water.

Cooper pulled out the brush. He touched it to his paper. But the paint had washed off! The brush made only clear, wet marks. No sun. Cooper felt sad.

His teacher came over. "Let's fix that," she said softly. She gave him a fresh cup of paint. Cooper dipped his brush in. Now the yellow came back! He made a big round sun.

Then he dipped the brush in the glass of water. He touched it to the paper. A soft yellow puddle spread out. Cooper laughed. "It's a sun with rain!"
